messages:
sarah: Heads up — after the microbatch-window tweak rolled last night we saw a big p99 tail spike in prod. baseline p99 ~420ms, spike to ~1.3s for a ~20m window starting 02:12 UTC. Looks correlated with mass KV eviction bursts under ~1k concurrent sessions.

anil: ack. do you have the eviction/kv metrics and a small trace?

sarah: pasted snippets below (sanitized):

```
# snapshot @ 2026-03-14T02:13:45Z
concurrency=980
microbatch.target=8
microbatch.max=32
kernel.selected=attn_v3_fast
evictions/sec=850
kv_cache_size=78%  # capacity percent
kv_miss_rate=0.18
p95=210ms p99=1.3s
cpu.user=17% gpu.util=63%
```

sarah: Also saw repeated logs: `kv: evict shard=12 range=0x7f.. count=256 reason=pressure` and a few `kernel fallback to attn_v2` when sequences hit longer tails.

evan: interesting — sounds like synchronized eviction (cache-slam). When microbatch window grows we combine more requests but also extend per-request KV lifetimes? could push eviction churn when many sessions have interleaved prefixes.

perf-ci: ran a quick local replay with the same concurrency and microbatch settings. Reproducer command: `./tools/loadgen --concurrency 1000 --qps 1200 --microbatch-target 8 --seq-dist const:64`. Observed similar p99 jump and eviction bursts. I captured a perf flame and heap diff: https://perf.internal/flows/rep-1852104321 (flamegraph shows ~32% time in kv eviction loop during spike).

anya: a few thoughts:
- eviction churn increases KV access latency and can invalidate hot KV entries mid-request, which forces kernel to rewarm the KV and sometimes pick slower fallback kernels.
- kernel selection appears influenced by sequence length distribution + kv miss penalty. If miss rate spikes the heuristics choose a more conservative kernel.

anil: agree. short-term mitigations?
- lower microbatch.max to reduce simultaneous KV lifetimes (try max=16)
- add jitter to KV eviction threshold so we don't evict many shards at once (randomized TTL/threshold)
- force kernel pin for the affected model (temp) to avoid fallback thrash
- bump cache capacity for the model group if possible (config)

sarah: doing a phased roll: (1) toggle microbatch.max -> 16 on canary pool (2) enable randomized eviction jitter (3) pin kernel to attn_v2 for canary. Will monitor p95/p99.

deploy-bot: deploy started for bucket `canary-evict-1852` at 2026-03-14T03:05:12Z

perf-ci: after canary swap (10% traffic) we saw p99 drop from 1.3s -> 480ms and evictions/sec down 6x. Good sign. Need 50% ramp to be confident.

evan: we should also consider a longer-term fix in kernel selection heuristics: incorporate recent kv_miss_rate as a factor so we don't pick an aggressive kernel when miss penalty is high. Also add a circuit-breaker that prevents global kernel roll on short-term miss spikes.

anya: agreed. action items:
- anil: implement eviction jitter and safe defaults (PR + perf test) — due EOD Wed
- sarah: finish 50% canary ramp and post metrics (p95/p99, evictions/sec, kernel-change events)
- evan: design kernel-selection tweak proposal (include kv_miss_rate) — tech spec by Fri
- perf-ci: add synthetic test for cache-slam scenario in ci/perf (so we catch regressions)

anil: quick question — what about microbatch sizing heuristic? current algo upsizes aggressively based on qps; maybe change to be KV-aware (don't increase if kv_cache_fill > 70%).

sarah: good idea. I'll record that as a follow-up. For now, canary rollback is planned if p99 > 600ms for 10min window.

perf-ci: note added testcases and a reproducer script at `tools/repro/cache_slam_repro.sh`. Example usage: `./cache_slam_repro.sh --concurrency 1000 --microbatch 8,32 --duration 600s`

sarah: thanks team. I'll update here with 50% canary results in ~30m. :white_check_mark:

anil: thanks — also cc @ops for a heads-up if we need capacity bump.

sarah: 50% canary summary: p99 steady ~520ms, evictions/sec ~120, kv_miss 0.05. Rolling to 100% after 20m observation window.

evan: great. let's still keep the kernel-selection change and eviction jitter on the roadmap.

sarah: closing thread once 100% finish. thanks all. :party_popper:
